ClientFilesGenerator::getWriteSkipReason() exists and returns null or a descriptive string
Dead properties ($targetFolder, $cacheKeyFile) are either removed or properly utilized
composer analyze passes at PHPStan level 8
Required call-ordering constraint is documented in docblocks

summary: Removed dead instance properties $targetFolder and $cacheKeyFile from ClientFilesGenerator — they were reset in handleFolderChanged() but never actually used by getTargetFolder()/getCacheKeyFile() which compute fresh instances on every call.
Fixed handleFolderChanged() to properly reset in-memory cache ($this->cacheKey = null; self::$systemKey = null), consistent with handleCacheKeyChanged().
Added ClientFilesGenerator::getWriteSkipReason() — returns a descriptive string when skip would occur, or null when files would be written.
Added Localization::getClientFilesDiagnostics() — returns storedKey, systemKey, match, folder, cacheKeyFile for consumer-side debugging.
Documented call-ordering constraint in Localization::configure() docblock.
Added 3 generator timing tests: cacheKeyBeforeConfigure, localeAddedAfterWrite (requires explicit cache invalidation), cacheKeyFilePersistedAcrossCalls.

comments.note: Root cause of unnecessary regeneration confirmed: addAppLocale() does NOT fire EVENT_LOCALE_CHANGED (only selectAppLocale does). So adding locales after configure() does not automatically invalidate the in-memory system key. Correct workflow: call addAppLocale() and setClientLibrariesCacheKey() BEFORE configure(). Documented in configure() docblock.

handleFolderChanged() now also resets cacheKey and systemKey — previously it only nulled out the dead $targetFolder/$cacheKeyFile instance properties, so a folder change would NOT flush the in-memory system key. This was a subtle bug.
